mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each individual UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the country of origin; notarized by a public notary/commissioner for oaths in that jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO proof of residential address (bank statement, utility bill, or government notice dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank, utility provider, or government authority; notarized by a licensed notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing/corporate status extract for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the entity's formation jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds (required in enhanced due diligence or PEP-linked cases)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the shareholder/UBO, authenticated by bank seal and notarized signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French or English translation of all notarized foreign-language documents submitted for Quebec corporate records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where the underlying notarized instrument requires it

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against FINTRAC requirements under the PCMLTFA and its regulations; Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists; regulations made under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act; and the foreign public officials regime under the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Because Stripe and PayPal clear USD transactions, OFAC SDN screening and the OFAC 50% ownership rule are also applied. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, and senior management approval. All screening records must be retained at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Name Analysis and Reservation Service (online at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in French under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11. A non-French name is permitted only if a French version is also provided with at least equal prominence in the register. Only Latin-script characters and standard French diacritics are accepted; no pictographic or non-Latin corporate name forms are registered. The legal element must be a permitted form such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or its French equivalent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed or replaced before expiry; after expiry a new name request is required. If the Registraire rejects the name, the incorporator may file a written administrative reconsideration within 30 days of the refusal explaining compliance with the language rules and absence of misrepresentation. If the reconsideration is denied, an application for judicial review may be made to the Superior Court of Quebec under article 529 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The applicant may simultaneously file a fresh name application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For this low-risk non-licensed print-on-demand retail activity, a Quebec virtual office is acceptable as the registered office under the Business Corporations Act provided it is a real physical address in Quebec, is attended during normal business hours, and is able to receive service of process. The virtual-office provider contract must expressly allow inspection and legal service, and the company must still maintain books and records at an accessible Quebec location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 2-5% probability over the first 36 months for a non-licensed, low-risk e-commerce corporation with timely GST/QST filings. Unannounced physical inspections are possible by Revenu Quebec or the Registraire des entreprises if red flags arise, such as apparent inactive office, unreported revenue, sanctions/PEP matching, or repeat chargebacks, which could materially increase the probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 2, 20, 34, 64 and Part II; read with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 25-40
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under QBCA s. 34; shares may be issued without an escrow account or paid-up capital at formation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) the Corporation adopts its Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and ratifies the allotment and issuance of common shares to the subscriber evidenced in the share subscription agreement; (2) the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [address], Province of Quebec, where statutory records shall be maintained; (3) the directors adopt the Corporation's operating by-laws and open the primary corporate bank account, designating the President and Secretary as joint signing officers; (4) the following officers be and are hereby appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer; (5) the officers are authorized to complete ancillary filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Revenu Québec and the Canada Revenue Agency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Online Name Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request online through REQ's enterprise file portal, providing up to three proposed legal names in order of preference with a descriptive statement of business activities, and pay the name research fee; REQ issues a name search certificate once the proposed name is declared distinct and lawful under QBCA rules.
required_dossiers: Payment record of name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, resubmit an amended request with alternative names within 30 days or adopt a number-name (e.g., 1234-5678 Québec Inc.), which is issued automatically by REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Corporate Services Counter / Online filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the Articles of Incorporation electronically under Part II of the QBCA, specifying share structure, share categories, transfer restrictions, first directors' names and addresses, and the registered office address; attach the name search certificate and pay the CAD 345 online filing fee; REQ processes the filing and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the Québec enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: List of first directors with consent to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a deficiency notice, correct the flagged items and resubmit within 30 days; the original filing date is preserved if the corrected version is delivered within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of By-laws and Establishment of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Corporate Secretary (internal governance; no REQ filing unless an annual declaration update is required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational board meeting or execute a unanimous written resolution adopting the general by-laws under QBCA s. 64, fixing the registered office, appointing officers, issuing shares reflected in the share register, and authorizing banking resolutions; record all actions in the statutory minute book and share certificate register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate records are later challenged by a bank or third party, ratify the by-laws and share issuances by a subsequent board resolution and update the minute book retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with CRA and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — Mon dossier entreprise
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) with GST/HST account (RT), corporate income tax account (RC), and payroll deductions account (RP) if employees are hired; then register with Revenu Québec for the QST account, applying voluntarily if annual taxable sales are below CAD 30,000 to recover input tax refunds; finalize the registrations with the company's registered office and officers' identifiers.
required_dossiers: Identity and authorization documents of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registration is rejected for identity mismatch, resubmit with the corporate authorization form (NR1) and supporting board resolution; accounts are activated retroactively once the corrected filings are accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (applicable Ville) and Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ); CNESST for occupational health and safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal commercial business permit at the location of the registered office or fulfillment studio, obtain an RBQ conformity attestation for the commercial occupancy, and register with CNESST as an employer; secure municipal fire safety certification before commencing activities.
required_dossiers: RBQ attestation of conformity if premises occupied
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the permit, remediate the zoning or fire-safety violation and re-file the application; an appeal to the municipal council is available within 30 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation Registry Compliance and Annual Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure REQ records remain current by filing the annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) no later than the anniversary month of incorporation, updating directors, registered office, activity codes, and corporate information; this maintains the NEQ in good standing and prevents registry dissolution.
required_dossiers: Updated director and registered office information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is late, file immediately online and pay the late fee (CAD 35-190 depending on delay); if a dissolution notice has issued, apply for revocation of dissolution under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) — not applicable to POD e-commerce retail (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 454110); relevant only if the company installs a screen-printing or textile production plant
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial industrial operating license required for Print-on-Demand custom apparel retail; only a municipal commercial permit is required if a physical storefront or production studio is operated

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — POD e-commerce retail is outside Schedule I of the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23); a certificate of authorization is required only if textile printing activities discharge trade effluent or emit over 1 tonne/year of VOCs
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered at formation; if a printing studio is added, municipal sewer limits apply (pH 6.0–9.5, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 600 mg/L), VOC thresholds under the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1), and ink/solvent disposal under the Residual Materials Management Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 19)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CNESST workplace registration and workers' compensation coverage; municipal fire safety inspection certificate; RBQ structural load and electrical conformity clearance for commercial occupancy under the Construction Code

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Quebec-specific: Revenu Québec – https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident entities carrying on business in Canada must register for a federal Business Number (BN) with CRA using the Business Registration Online (BRO) service or Form RC1. The BN is a nine-digit unique identifier. For GST/HST, the BN with an 'RT' program account suffix serves as the GST/HST registration number. For Quebec, a separate QST registration number must be obtained from Revenu Québec. Documentation includes proof of incorporation in the home jurisdiction, identification of directors, and information on Canadian activities. Registration is required if worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a fiscal year, or if other registration triggers apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – a Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer under the federal Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act. It is not a pass-through entity; profits are taxed at the corporate level, and dividends are taxed separately on shareholders. Federal and Quebec provincial corporate tax rates apply, with a preferential rate for Canadian-controlled private corporations where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' or entity classification election is available under Canadian federal or Quebec law. Tax classification is determined by statute and legal form. Certain elections exist (e.g., s.216 rental income election, associated corporations allocation), but they do not alter entity classification. Hybrid mismatch rules (ITA s.12.6, s.18.4) disallow deductions for certain hybrid instruments; no elective mitigation is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Excise Tax Act (federal) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax; administered concurrently by CRA and Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies (excluding capital property, zero-rated exports) for both GST/HST and QST; applicable to POD retailers once threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance for B2B or B2C transactions. Electronic invoicing is permitted if it satisfies CRA and Revenu Québec evidentiary requirements; no continuous transaction controls, API requirements, or digital stamping are statutorily required. B2B e-invoicing mandates are anticipated but not yet implemented.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada by the supplier qualify as zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act, provided they are delivered to a non-resident outside Canada and proof of export is retained. For POD custom apparel shipped to a foreign customer via a commercial carrier, the supply is zero-rated. Services supplied to a non-resident that are performed entirely outside Canada may also qualify. The supplier must maintain documentary evidence to substantiate the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (G13/Exit) or commercial invoice with customs proof
Bill of Lading / airway bill or courier tracking evidence of export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer receipt for foreign currency settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may audit zero-rated export claims retrospectively for up to four years (longer in cases of misrepresentation). Improper zero-rating results in assessment of uncollected GST/QST, interest, penalties of 10% of net tax, and up to 50% of the tax for negligence. Fraudulent claims can lead to criminal prosecution with fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment. Anti-avoidance rules under the Excise Tax Act apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central monetary authority) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the prudential banking regulator; Canada does not maintain a separate foreign-exchange control authority or exchange-control licensing board.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible. Canada maintains no exchange-control legislation, no restrictions on current-account transactions, and no restrictions on capital-account transactions. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, repatriation of capital, and intercompany payments may be freely effected in Canadian dollars or any foreign currency, subject only to standard corporate solvency and dividend-eligibility rules under the Canada Business Corporations Act and the Quebec Business Corporations Act. No prior central-bank approval, foreign-exchange license, or repatriation tax clearance is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank or any government authority. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency, converted at any authorized financial institution, or used directly for settlement of foreign-currency liabilities at the discretion of the exporter.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (National Bank / BNC)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability. Foreign electronic money institutions and non-resident fintech payment service providers are not permitted to take deposits or carry on deposit-taking business in Canada without being authorized as a bank, a federal credit union, or a payment service provider registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Offshore digital EMIs may offer payment facilitation through Canadian partner banks or local money-services-business licensees, but a Quebec-based operating entity should primarily rely on regulated Canadian Schedule I banks and authorized payment processors for treasury clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for corporate account opening under Canadian AML/KYC rules. Canadian banks may permit remote onboarding using video-identification procedures, notarized identification packages, or reliance on recognized correspondent-bank due diligence, subject to enhanced monitoring. However, in practice, directors or authorized signatories may be required to attend an initial in-branch or video-conference interview with corporate banking compliance officers, particularly where the company is newly incorporated, has non-resident ownership, or anticipates high cross-border payment volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or remote directors and ultimate beneficial owners without Canadian credit or banking history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies; proof of residential address; corporate registry extracts from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; notarized certificate of incumbency; a corporate resolution appointing the account signatories; and a clear organizational chart identifying all ultimate beneficial owners with ownership percentages.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume commerce payment flows through third-party payment aggregators such as Stripe and PayPal rather than direct merchant processing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform services agreements; merchant identification numbers; settlement statements; historical transaction summaries; a written explanation of the POD order-to-settlement flow; and confirmation that all payouts are attributable to bona fide retail sales of custom apparel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Print-on-demand business classification perceived as high-risk due to cross-border e-commerce and unknown end consumers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product catalog; sample invoices; supplier contracts with POD fulfillment partners; website terms of sale; refund and dispute resolution policies; and evidence of compliance with Quebec consumer protection statutes and Canadian anti-money-laundering reporting obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected large inbound capital contributions from foreign shareholders or related-party loans for working capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder loan agreements or subscription agreements; board resolutions authorizing the capital injection; source-of-funds declarations supported by bank statements; and tax advice confirming the treatment of contributed surplus or intercompany indebtedness.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of corporate escrow or reserve accounts for future payments or capital preservation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow agreement or treasury policy; reconciliation procedures; independent accounting review; and a written attestation that escrowed funds do not constitute prohibited deposit-taking activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the remitting entity to the Quebec corporation's Canadian-dollar operating account at a Schedule I bank. The wire should carry a clear ISO 20022 remittance information field describing the transaction as 'share capital contribution', 'contributed surplus', or 'non-resident shareholder loan', supported by corporate resolutions and subscription documents. Canada has no central-bank foreign-exchange purpose-code regime and does not require prior approval for inward FDI; however, the receiving bank may request a source-of-funds declaration, the Quebec corporate registry extract, and beneficial-ownership confirmation to satisfy FINTRAC and OSFI guidance. Large settlements may additionally require the remitting institution to use its Canadian correspondent bank and the Payments Canada Lynx settlement system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and fulfillment payments should use SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wire transfers, with commercial letters of credit presented via SWIFT MT700/MT707 where the POD supplier requires documentary assurance. Canadian-dollar domestic disbursements clear through Payments Canada's Lynx real-time gross settlement system or the Real-Time Rail for faster retail payments. United States dollar payments to POD fulfillment partners may be settled through Canadian banks' US clearing correspondents or through the Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS) / Fedwire using a US-dollar operating account. All outbound wires must include accurate payment descriptions covering inventory purchases, fulfillment fees, shipping costs, duty remittances, and service fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR)
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and other convertible currency pairs)
Vanilla FX options (call and put options on CAD)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid or restricted emerging-market currencies where convertibility or settlement limitations exist
Currency futures traded on recognized Canadian or international exchanges
Foreign-currency bank accounts and natural hedging through multi-currency operating accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle du Registre des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Ministère de la Justice du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's Quebec registration or incorporation; filed online through the clicSÉEQ portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee accrues after the 60-day deadline, up to CAD 500 per declaration; failure to file for at least 12 consecutive months permits REQ to issue a notice and administratively dissolve (strike-off) the corporation under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), subject to a notice period to remedy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act, including beneficial ownership information for individuals with significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; beneficial ownership information is mandatory for all annual returns due on or after January 22, 2024
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A CAD 100 late filing fee applies to returns submitted after the 60-day window; failure to file for one year or more allows the Director to dissolve the corporation administratively under CBCA s. 212 after a 120-day notice; reinstatement requires court or Director approval with payment of arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; federal income tax balance due within 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs and within 3 months for Canadian-controlled private corporations, with quarterly instalments when prescribed thresholds are exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; repeated-filing penalty; gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax; prescribed-rate interest on unpaid amounts; potential director liability for unremitted withholdings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return (CO-17) and accompanying schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; Quebec income tax balance due within 2 or 3 months after year-end according to CCPC status; instalment obligations mirror the federal regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to a 12-month maximum; prescribed-rate interest on late or deficient instalments; enforcement measures under the Quebec Taxation Act, including director liability assessments and seizure procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or balance-sheet-based audit threshold applies to non-distributing private corporations under the CBCA (R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44) or the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c. S-31.1). An independent licensed auditor must be appointed at each annual shareholders' meeting unless every shareholder consents in writing each year to waive the appointment. Distributing (public) corporations and corporations subject to specific regulated-industry rules are always subject to mandatory audit and audit committee requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook – Part I). Private corporations may elect IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook – Part II). Print-on-demand e-commerce revenue is recognized under IFRS 15 or ASPE Section 3400 as applicable. Books and records must be maintained in Canadian dollars with a complete audit trail.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each annual declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec must confirm the corporation's significant beneficial owners, being individuals holding at least 25% of voting rights or possessing de facto control. The internal transparency register must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer that alters significant-owner positions. Under the CBCA, the register of individuals with significant control must likewise be updated within 15 days of a transfer, and the beneficial ownership details are transmitted to Corporations Canada with the federal annual return. Share transfers must also be recorded in the share-transfer ledger with cancelled and reissued certificates properly noted.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders ledger including share transfers and issued certificates)
Register of Directors (appointments, resignations, addresses, and occupation)
Minute Book (constating documents, by-laws, directors' and shareholders' minutes and resolutions)
Register of Significant Beneficial Owners (CBCA s. 32.1 and Quebec transparency register requirements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–450 per year (CAD 200–600) for commercial registered-office and registered-agent services in Montreal or Quebec City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500–10,500 (CAD 5,000–15,000) for a full Canadian CPA statutory audit of a small print-on-demand retail corporation; compilation or review engagement typically USD 1,300–4,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (federal general rate 15% after the 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction; Quebec general corporate rate 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD): first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) taxed at 9% federally and 3.2% in Quebec (combined 12.2%), subject to phase-out where taxable capital exceeds CAD 15 million; SR&ED refundable investment tax credit (35% for qualifying CCPCs) and provincial research credits; immediate expensing of eligible Canadian manufacturing/processing and clean-energy equipment; no industry-specific tax holiday for retail e-commerce or POD activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: Form T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, accompanied by GIFI (T2 Schedule 125) financial statements and T2 Schedules 1, 4, 8 and 9; filed electronically through CRA My Business Account or GIFI-certified EFILE software (mandatory for most corporations)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one T2 per taxation year; quarterly instalments of corporate tax, not quarterly returns)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 due no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end; final tax balance due 2 months after year-end (3 months for CCPCs claiming the SBD); Part XIII non-resident withholding remitted monthly by the 15th day of the following month; instalments paid per the corporation's instalment schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Page 1 - Identification (name, Business Number/RC account, incorporation jurisdiction, fiscal period, RZ digit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, CRA 9-digit Business Number and RZ program digit, date and jurisdiction of incorporation (federal or Quebec), registered office address and taxation year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations without a Canadian permanent establishment (PE) are generally outside the T2 filing net and file Part XIII returns instead; where a PE exists, identify the provincial allocation factors in Schedule 5

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting income before tax reconciled to income under the Income Tax Act; POD gross receipts from Stripe/PayPal classified as revenue, net of chargebacks, payment-processor commissions and cost of goods sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Canadian-source income attributable to the PE is recognized; platform commissions and merchant fees must be deducted in accordance with s.18(1)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income minus non-capital loss carryovers, capital cost allowance (CCA) and allowable business investment losses to arrive at taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute taxable income solely from the PE's Canadian business; DTA provisions (e.g., Canada-US Article VII) limit the PE profit attribution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 300-330 (base tax, provincial abatement and general rate reduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 300 federal base rate 38%; Line 320 provincial abatement 10%; Line 330 general rate reduction 13%, yielding the 15% general federal rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Part I tax of a non-resident corporation is computed on PE income with the same abatement mechanics; the abatement applies only where provincial tax allocation is made

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SBD claimed on active business income up to the federal CAD 500,000 limit, allocated among associated CCPCs and reduced above CAD 15 million taxable capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled corporations do not qualify as CCPCs and cannot claim the SBD; Part VII/VIII refundable tax and RDTOH schedules apply where investment income exists

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 9 (cross-border transactions) and Form T106
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with related non-resident suppliers, POD platform providers, licensees or IP holders
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for a Canadian corporation transacting with non-resident related parties above CAD 1,000,000 (non-loan) or CAD 5,000,000 (loan) in the year

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late-filing penalty under s.162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; additional 10% penalty for a second or subsequent failure; s.163(2) gross-negligence penalty equal to 50% of understated tax; s.161 arrears interest accrues daily at the CRA prescribed rate (approximately 8-9% in 2024) on both late balances and instalments; criminal prosecution under s.239 for wilful late filing
